rules: Correlate a volume series with a range or a change, not with a raw price level, and keep the correlation window at 21 days or longer: TS_CORR of volume against ($high - $low) or against TS_DELTA($volume, 1) over 21 to 42 days produced every accept above 3.0, while TS_CORR($volume, $high, 21) failed the cheap screen at |t| 0.57 and a 5-day TS_CORR of two TS_RANKs reached only 1.13.

Pair a fundamental spread (roe, roa, accrual_gap, leverage) with a volume/range correlation leg, which scored 4.14 and 5.23. The same spreads multiplied by return momentum (TS_SUM($return, 68)) or by a price-level ratio scored |t| 0.41 and 0.09 on the cheap screen.

Stop proposing a cross-sectional fundamental rank times a plain price-level ratio (mean high over mean low, $open over VWAP, book per share over price). All four such proposals died on the cheap screen at |t| 0.09 to 0.54; normalise the price leg into a range or a change first.

To clear the correlation gate against archive fundamentals, change the fundamental field itself. Re-encoding CS_RANK(a) - CS_RANK(b) as CS_ZSCORE(a - b), or swapping one liquidity proxy for another (LOG dollar_volume for a range sum), left |rho| at 0.82 to 0.84 against existing members.

Two blocks are now archived subtrees and trip the subtree gate even under a new wrapper: the intraday pressure term ($high - $open) - ($open - $low), and a range divided by a 21-day mean price. Rebuild that normaliser from different fields if the idea is still wanted.

Five rejected mutations drifted 4 to 7 edits from the parent, mostly by bolting on a whole normalised second leg or by changing wrapper, window, and field together. Change one field or one window per proposal.
Do not stack a 252-day TS_RANK on top of a 63-day fundamental delta; that lookback chain lost coverage at 0.841. The accepted leverage factor used the 63-day delta with no outer long window.

Spend extra nodes on a second data field rather than on branching or deeper wrapping. The two weakest accepts (0.649 and 1.263) spent them on SIGN and on an IF_ELSE threshold, and every accept above 3.0 came from a low-complexity niche.
